messages:
alex: Heads-up — PR open to change the reserved_gpu module input surface. Splitting kms_key_id -> kms {primary_key, fallback_key} and replacing iam_role string -> iam_boundary map. Marking as v2. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/pulls/432. Plan shows aws_kms_alias replacement for some gpupools, want eyes on drift impact.
marta: Does this require recreating instances or draining pools? Which resources get replaced exactly?
alex: Only aws_kms_alias and the IAM policy resource appear as 'replace' in the plan. No EC2/EKS node replacements expected. Biggest operational risk is GitOps diffs for customers who pass top-level strings today.
raj: Can we add a backwards-compatible shim so current consumers don't break on module upgrade? e.g., accept both string and map for iam_boundary and keep kms_key_id as deprecated var with a warning. Maybe a migration flag to auto-migrate alias naming.
jiayi: Agreed on shim. Also callout: provider version skew (aws provider) is causing plan noise — terraform 1.5 vs 1.6 in CI leads to different alias handling. We should lock provider or run consistent container in the gitops runner.
alex: Prototype shim snippet I'm testing:
```hcl
variable "iam_boundary" {
  description = "legacy string or new map {name, path, account}"
  type = any
}
locals {
  iam_boundary_map = can(var.iam_boundary) && (type(var.iam_boundary) == map(string)) ? var.iam_boundary : {name = tostring(var.iam_boundary)}
}
```
Will also emit a deprecation notice via `null_resource` local-exec to surface in plan.
oliver: Also suggest region-gated canary. Some eu-west-1 customers still use older fleet images and our autoscaler tagging is different there. Canary to 3 reserved pools in us-west-2 first.
infra-bot: ci:tf-plan result for pr/432 — 3 workspaces with diffs, 1 workspace requires manual apply. Details: https://ci.redwood/internal/plans/432
marta: :thumbsup: Proposed rollout: 1) implement shim and keep v2 backwards-compatible, 2) publish changelog and note deprecation, 3) canary apply to us-west-2 reserved pools, 4) monitor autoscaler and KPIs (scale-up latency, failed allocations) for 48h, 5) flip to strict input validation in next release after customers migrate.
raj: Also add a check in our gitops runner: when a repo bumps module to v2, append a migration note to the PR body and tag infra-oncall automatically. Saves repeated triage when we get noisy plan failures.
jiayi: I'll add provider lockfile updates and a CI job that runs `terraform 1.6 plan` in the canonical container to reduce plan drift. Will also add tflint to the pipeline.
alex: Thanks all — I'll push the shim commit and update the PR with the canary playbook. Will tag @oncall during the canary apply so SRE can watch the autoscaler dashboards.
